## 4\. Strengthening the construction to polynomial numerical coefficient heights

There is one additional resource issue worth eliminating. The cosine-power construction (1) has polynomial *binary* coefficient lengths, but its Fourier denominators can be exponentially large as integers.

To satisfy even the stricter interpretation that the numerators and denominators themselves must be polynomially bounded in \(R\), use the following modification. **This is the final algorithm for the full resource contract.**

Keep

\[
A_0=R^{100},\qquad n=R^{200},
\]

but set

\[
M=R^6,\qquad N=2M+1
\]

and define the normalized Dirichlet polynomial

\[
D_M(\theta)=
\frac{1+2\sum_{j=1}^{M}\cos(2\pi j\theta)}{2M+1}.
\]

Define the nonnegative localization kernel

\[
J_M(\theta)=D_M(\theta)^{32}.
\]

Replace every \(P_m\) in Section 1 by \(J_M\), obtaining

\[
\begin{aligned}
v_1&=J_M(y)\big[J_M(z)-J_M(z-\tfrac12)\big],\\
v_2&=\big[J_M(x)-J_M(x-\tfrac12)\big]J_M(z-\tfrac14),\\
v_3&=\big[J_M(x-\tfrac14)-J_M(x-\tfrac34)\big]J_M(y-\tfrac14).
\end{aligned}
\tag{4}
\]

The final controller is

\[
\boxed{b(x)=nA_0v(nx).}
\tag{5}
\]

This has the same channel geometry but better exact coefficient bounds.

### Exact arithmetic properties

Because

\[
D_M(\theta)=\frac1N\sum_{j=-M}^{M}e^{2\pi ij\theta},
\]

the coefficients of \(J_M\) have denominator \(N^{32}\) and integer numerators bounded by \(N^{32}\)\.

Each component of \(v\) is a sum of at most two products of such kernels. Consequently, after multiplication by \(nA_0\), the absolute numerator and denominator of every Fourier coefficient are bounded by

\[
10nA_0N^{64}
\leq 10\cdot3^{64}R^{684}.
\]

In particular, **even the unlogged rational coefficient height is polynomial in \(R\)**\.

Also,

\[
0\leq J_M\leq1,\qquad
\deg J_M\leq32M.
\]

The shifts by quarters preserve rational trigonometric coefficients.

---

## 5\. Quantitative geometry: variance without significant self-advection

The following estimates hold for the field (4)\:

\[
\boxed{
\begin{aligned}
\|v\|_\infty&\leq2,\\
\|\nabla v\|_\infty&\leq10^4M,\\
\|\Delta v\|_\infty&\leq10^6M^2,\\
\|(v\cdot\nabla)v\|_\infty&\leq10^{12}M^{-30}.
\end{aligned}
}
\tag{6}
\]

Furthermore, for every Euclidean unit vector \(e\in\mathbb R^3\),

\[
\boxed{
\int_{\mathbb T^3}(e\cdot v)^2\,dx
\geq\alpha:=10^{-12}M^{-2}.
}
\tag{7}
\]
